question: Can committed joint paths create useful intermediate solutions beyond known endpoints, more efficiently than one-shot joint crossover?
sampling: All6existing pre-batch CENTER windows,8equally spaced freeCENTER parents per window; freeM/E/W donors floor(i*10/7) within the11current members. No quality-based donor or window selection.144pairs but48recipient clusters perinstance.
construction: Commit each targetJS job: put job at its target absolute position by a job-aligned swap, transfer its fullFA/MA/WA. If this empties a factory, transfer smallest-id uncommitted job targeting that factory, until coverage restored. Each auxiliary transfer corrects another targetFA; committed positions/tuples remain fixed. Endpoints match known teacher.
controls: REPAIR_PATH same commit order but ordinary common repair; laststep restores target to match known endpoint, all restoration work charged. RANDOM_PATH same cover rule, uniformly shuffled commit order. CLASSIC Nindependent actualsetting0 offspring from same fixed endpoints. All methods Npaid candidates; no uncharged lookahead or suffix rollout. Copy, construction, generic repair and evaluation measured.

scoring: Joint conditional HV gain of all Nintermediates per method, not sum of single-point gains. Average3teacher roles per recipient;48clusters perinstance. Frozen normalization, ref1.5 primary and1.25/2sensitivity.
gate: Both instances>=24informative recipients; COVER_PATH mean union-addedHV>=10%overCLASSIC,>=5%overRANDOM_PATH,>=-1%overREPAIR_PATH; >=27/48recipient wins vsCLASSIC andvsRANDOM_PATH; both source seeds positive vsboth; eachstep aggregate nonnegative vsCLASSIC; reference1.25/2 directions vsCLASSIC/RANDOM_PATH positive. novelty: Ordinary path relinking is established. Cover chains are feasibility engineering, not an independent novelty claim; REPAIR_PATH near-equivalence would not establish special gain from cover. No claim four-role origin or fatigue adds independent value yet.
